''''' Erica australis''''', the '''Spanish heath''' or '''Southern tree heath''',<ref name=Proudley /> is a European [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Ericaceae.

It is a bushy [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|2|m|ft|abbr=off|frac=2}} tall and broad, with tiny needle-like [[leaves]] and pink to purple bell-shaped flowers in late spring. As a [[calcifuge]], it requires sharply drained acidic soil in full sun. It is hardy down to {{convert|-10|C|F|abbr=on}}.

The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''australis'' means 'southern', referring to its native habitat of southern Europe,<ref name="RHSLG">{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=184533731X }}</ref> including the western [[Iberian Peninsula]] ([[Portugal]] and Western [[Spain]]) as well as Northwest [[Africa]] (in [[Morocco]]).

This plant is cultivated as an ornamental and has produced numerous forms and [[cultivar]]s,<ref name=Proudley>{{cite book |author1=Brian Proudley |author2=Valerie Proudley |title=Heathers in Colour |date=1989 |publisher=Blandford Press |isbn=0713714204 |pages=143-144 |edition=2nd |quote=''Erica australis'' (Spanish heath, Southern tree heath) ... Although many fine plants are in cultivation ... we believe we have been able to increase the colour range available.}}</ref> gaining the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] for ''E. australis'' 'Mr Robert'.<ref>{{cite web
